cohort: 75 women aged ≥ 45 years who gave birth to twins, each matched to two women ≥ 45 years who gave birth to singletons within 7 days.
finding: Women ≥ 45 years of age with twin pregnancies experienced significantly more hypertensive complications, preeclamptic toxemia, preterm deliveries, and their infants had higher rates of low birth weight, very low birth weight, intubation, hypoglycemia, and NICU admissions compared to matched singletons.
birth_weight: Low birth weight and very low birth weight
